_comment: THE LOAD TEST'S LIMITS (DECISIONS #284; tests/load_test.sh, tools/load/load_test.py). A step of the test HOLDS when every limit here holds; the first step that does not is where the game breaks on this machine. A limit of null is measured and reported but not judged. A genre may override any of them in shared/<genre>/load.json (later genres win). The 'keeps up' limits are engineering facts: the movement tick runs 20 times a second, so a tick that takes longer than its 50 ms falls behind. The per-client bandwidth limits are a design budget (Luke's to set: null until he does). THE SERVER IS JUDGED BY ITS EXACT NUMBERS (template 1.5): 'module_busy_pct', how much of the window the module's one thread was busy (100 is the ceiling: 80 leaves room for a burst), and 'tick_movement_mean_ms', the movement tick's own mean (25: half its 50 ms, the rest for every other reducer). The p95s ('tick_movement_p95_ms', 'reducer_wait_p95_ms') are only as good as the server's buckets (1, 5, 10, 50 ms) and are reported, not judged. 'referee_gone_refusals' counts judged abilities refused because the referee had dropped out. 'level' is the level world 0 plays the test on (a LevelDef id; 0 the greybox): a game whose world is elsewhere sets it in its own load.json. 'referees' [columns, rows] cuts the bots' square into that many regions, a referee each (DECISIONS #288); [1, 1] is one referee for the whole world. 'spread' (template 1.5, tools/load/level.py): {"over": "square"} every bot anywhere in the area_cells square (the default); {"over": "level", "crowd_share": 0.2, "crowd_cells": 6, "roam_cells": 6} homes anywhere on the level's land (its bake), a share of them in a town round the spawn, each walking within roam_cells of home; the referees are then cut where the bots live. LOAD=<name> reads shared/<genre>/load_<name>.json over the game's load.json.
